output.brief: The evidence points to a single chance QC flag, not a fault with the analyzer or the new reagent lot. The repeat of the same QC material passed. The other QC levels and sodium and chloride were fine. Level 2 averages are unchanged since the lot change. All QC ran on schedule, so skipped QC is not supported. Patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed within 0.02 mmol/L on average, and the patient median is stable. This kind of flag is expected roughly once or twice a month. The Ward 6 high potassiums are split evenly between Analyzers A and B. They coincide with the tube outage, with longer transit times, and with four overflow renal patients. Delay in transit is plausible, but the other explanations aren't ruled out. No repeat samples have been requested. I am fairly confident (about 70-80%). I did not collect further evidence. What to sign off: return Analyzer B potassium to service. Close the 186-result review with no amendments. Don't recall about 2,900 results, quarantine the lot or widen the limits. Consider an extra Level 2 QC per shift for a week. Do not record a sampling glitch as the confirmed cause, because it can't be shown. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples, and push for the tube repair.
